title: typeof and type conversion
learningObjectives: Explain typeof and type conversion and use JavaScript values and operators predictably.

understand.concept: typeof returns a string describing the type category of a value, with some historical exceptions. JavaScript also converts values explicitly using String(), Number(), and Boolean(), while implicit coercion can occur in operators and comparisons.
understand.whyItMatters: Explicit conversion makes intent easier to read and reduces surprising results. Validate conversions because Number('hello') produces NaN rather than a useful number.
understand.analogy: Type conversion is like translating a value into a different representation; the result may need checking before use.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript coercion, equality, and reference semantics follow the language specification.

explain.narrative: The numeric string becomes a number, then String converts it back to text. Number.isNaN can help check failed numeric conversion.

examples.explanation: The numeric string becomes a number, then String converts it back to text. Number.isNaN can help check failed numeric conversion.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the values and results described.

practise.guidedTask: Convert user input into a number, check Number.isNaN, and display a helpful error for invalid input.
practise.independentTask: Write a short program using the concept with realistic values. Predict the output before running it and explain any surprising result.
hints: Inspect both value and typeof when needed.
Use explicit conversion and validate its result.
Avoid relying on implicit coercion in security-sensitive logic.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>typeof and type conversion</title></head><body>
<script>const raw='42';const quantity=Number(raw);const label=String(quantity);console.log(typeof raw,typeof quantity,label,Number.isNaN(quantity));</script>
</body></html>

questions.explanation: A non-numeric string converted with Number produces NaN.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable way to understand a value conversion?
options: Inspect the original value, converted value, and conversion result
questions.answer: Inspect the original value, converted value, and conversion result
questions.explanation: Explicitly checking conversion results prevents invalid values from silently entering later calculations.
